correctness.rationale: The assigned RESULT.md is correct under its exact quantifiers: arbitrary set Gamma and arbitrary nonempty A⊆Gamma, with L=P(Gamma), lattice homomorphisms to [-1,1], and density character in the Banach-lattice norm. Let alpha=x*(empty) and beta=x*(A) and U={x*:beta>alpha}. Every f,g between delta(empty) and delta(A) have f(x*)=g(x*)=alpha outside U; deleting those zero-difference points from any admissible multi-functional norm sum proves that restriction r preserves all pairwise distances on the interval (and r is contractive on FBL). For B⊆Gamma put B0=B∩A and B1=B\A. On U, meet preservation gives min(x*(B1),beta)=x*(empty)=alpha; monotonicity x*(B1)>=alpha and beta>alpha force x*(B1)=alpha. Join preservation and x*(B0)>=alpha then give x*(B)=max(x*(B0),alpha)=x*(B0). Thus all r(delta(B)) equal r(delta(B∩A)), so r(FBL<L>) lies in the norm closure of a vector lattice generated by at most |P(A)|=2^|A| functions. Rational finite lattice-linear expressions furnish a dense subset of cardinal <= max(aleph0,2^|A|); metric subspaces cannot have larger density. The interval transfers this upper bound by distance-preserving r. Proposition 4.3 supplies the matching lower bound from the 1-separated delta(C) for all C⊆A and from the nondegenerate real segment. The endpoint A=empty is correctly excluded (singleton interval), finite nonempty A gives aleph0, infinite A gives 2^|A|, even if Gamma larger. No finite enumeration, inaccessible premise or verifier log is treated as proof.

Thus the general structural theorems do not by themselves imply the exact density of the entire ambient order interval.

originality.rationale: Qualified best-of-knowledge originality. The focal 2026 paper poses the exact same natural power-set example but supplies only a general lower bound and its singleton case. Its Theorem 4.9 and the earlier induced-embedding work establish complemented sublattice structures, not the critical assertion that restriction to U eliminates every generator indexed by B outside the interval via B∩A. The submitted proof supplies that exact universal collapse and closes the upper bound for all A, even when Gamma is much larger. Three targeted Resultary searches returned the submitted finding itself as nearest match, not an independent earlier exact formula. The extension is close to the focal proof and is not credited for its known ingredients; unsurfaced older formulations remain a real priority risk.

value.rationale: This is a complete all-cardinal classification of a natural family of principal order intervals in FBL<P(Gamma)> singled out by the focal 2026 research. It closes the precise gap where Remark 4.5 records only 2^|A| as a lower bound, and shows the upper bound depends on the local Boolean algebra P(A) rather than the potentially much larger ambient P(Gamma). It distinguishes finite-A separability from exact 2^|A| density for every infinite A, with a structural explanation via the restriction-map generator collapse. The invariant and family are motivated independently by the published interval-density problem, not an arbitrary computational slice; no general Banach-lattice theorem or downstream application is asserted.
